## 1. Purpose

This notebook demonstrates the feasibility of the regional skills-gap early-warning
system proposed in the project report. It uses **Electricians (ANZSCO 3411)** as a
worked example occupation, combining:

- **Demand side**: Jobs and Skills Australia's Internet Vacancy Index (IVI), monthly
  online job advertisement counts (reported as a three-month moving average) by
  occupation and JSA Remoteness classification.
- **Supply side**: NCVER's Total VET students and courses 2025 program completions,
  for the Electrotechnology (UEE, UTE, UTL) training package, by remoteness region.

Both datasets are publicly available. Download links and access notes are provided
in Section 2.

## 3. Loading and reshaping the data

### 3.1 Internet Vacancy Index (demand side)

```{r load-ivi}
# Source files are hosted in the project's public GitHub repository.
base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CR-28/FIT5145-A3-skills-gap-demo/main/data/"
ivi_file  <- "internet_vacancies_anzsco4_occupations_jsa_remoteness_and_northern_australia_classification_-_august_2026.xlsx"
ncver_file <- "Total_VET_students_and_courses_2025.xlsx"

# Use a local copy in data/ if one exists; otherwise download the file to a temp location.
get_data_file <- function(file_name) {
  local_path <- file.path("data", file_name)
  if (file.exists(local_path)) return(local_path)
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
  download.file(paste0(base_url, file_name), destfile = tmp, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  tmp
}

ivi_path <- get_data_file(ivi_file)

ivi_raw <- read_excel(ivi_path, sheet = "JSA Remoteness", col_names = TRUE)

# Filter to Electricians (ANZSCO 3411), reshape from wide (one column per month)
# to long format, and derive calendar year from the Excel date serial number.
elec_ivi <- ivi_raw %>%
  filter(ANZSCO_CODE == "3411") %>%
  select(-Level, -ANZSCO_CODE, -ANZSCO_TITLE) %>%
  rename(remoteness = `JSA Remoteness`) %>%
  pivot_longer(-remoteness, names_to = "date_serial", values_to = "vacancies") %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(as.numeric(date_serial), origin = "1899-12-30"),
    year = year(date)
  )
```

```{r show-elec-ivi, echo=FALSE}
elec_ivi %>% select(remoteness, date, vacancies) %>% head(6) %>%
  kable(caption = "Table 2: First 6 rows of reshaped IVI data (long format)", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"',
        format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

### 3.2 Exploratory check: data coverage

```{r eda-ivi}
# Check monthly coverage is complete (no missing months) before aggregating to
# annual totals - an incomplete year would bias the annual sum downward.
coverage <- elec_ivi %>%
  filter(year >= 2019, year <= 2025) %>%
  count(remoteness, year, name = "n_months") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = remoteness, values_from = n_months)
```

```{r show-coverage, echo=FALSE}
coverage %>% mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Table 3: Monthly data coverage check (should be 12 for every year)", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"') %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

```{r plot-raw, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(elec_ivi, aes(x = date, y = vacancies, colour = remoteness)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Raw monthly Electrician vacancies, by remoteness",
       x = NULL, y = "Online job ads", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Every year from 2019-2025 has a full 12 months of data for both regions, so no
interpolation or exclusion is needed before aggregating to annual totals. The raw
series shows clear COVID-era volatility (a sharp 2020 dip, then a steep 2021-2022
rebound), which motivates using **year-over-year growth rates** rather than raw
levels for comparison with completions - growth rates make the two series comparable 
even though they are measured in different units (online advertisements versus 
completions).

```{r annual-ivi}
ivi_annual <- elec_ivi %>%
  filter(year >= 2019, year <= 2025) %>%
  group_by(remoteness, year) %>%
  summarise(vacancies = sum(vacancies), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r show-ivi-annual, echo=FALSE}
ivi_annual %>% pivot_wider(names_from = remoteness, values_from = vacancies) %>%
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Table 4: Annual Electrician vacancies by remoteness, 2019-2025", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"',
        format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

**Note on the IVI values:** JSA reports the IVI as a three-month moving average of
advertisements on three major online job boards. Summing the twelve monthly values for a
year therefore gives a smoothed approximation of the annual advertisement count, not an
exact total. Because the same treatment is applied to every year and region, growth
rates remain comparable.

2026 is excluded as it is a partial year (data to August only) and would distort
a year-over-year growth calculation.

### 3.3 NCVER completions (supply side)

```{r load-ncver}
ncver_path <- get_data_file(ncver_file)

ncv_raw <- read_excel(ncver_path, sheet = "Pivot Data", col_names = FALSE)
header <- as.character(unlist(ncv_raw[1, ]))
data_rows <- ncv_raw[4:10, ]   # the 7 remoteness breakdown rows
colnames(data_rows) <- header

ncver_long <- data_rows %>%
  rename(training_package = 2, remoteness_ncver = 3) %>%
  select(-1) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(training_package, remoteness_ncver), names_to = "year", values_to = "completions") %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year), completions = as.numeric(completions))
```

```{r show-ncver-long, echo=FALSE}
ncver_long %>% select(-training_package) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = completions) %>%
  rename(Remoteness = remoteness_ncver) %>%
  kable(caption = "Table 5: Electrotechnology completions by remoteness region, 2019-2025", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"',
        format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

### 3.4 Harmonising geography

IVI classifies regions as a binary **Major City / Regional** split. NCVER's
DataBuilder exposes a finer 7-category remoteness classification. To join the two
datasets, the NCVER categories are collapsed as follows:

- `Major cities` -> **Major City**
- `Inner regional`, `Outer regional`, `Remote`, `Very remote` -> **Regional**
- `Offshore`, `Not known` -> **excluded** (together ~4.5% of total completions;
  these do not correspond to any IVI remoteness category and cannot be reliably
  allocated to either side of the binary split)

```{r harmonise}
ncver_annual <- ncver_long %>%
  mutate(remoteness = case_when(
    remoteness_ncver == "Major cities" ~ "Major City",
    remoteness_ncver %in% c("Inner regional", "Outer regional", "Remote", "Very remote") ~ "Regional",
    TRUE ~ "Exclude"
  )) %>%
  filter(remoteness != "Exclude") %>%
  group_by(remoteness, year) %>%
  summarise(completions = sum(completions), .groups = "drop")

excl_pct <- ncver_long %>%
  mutate(excl = remoteness_ncver %in% c("Offshore", "Not known")) %>%
  summarise(pct = 100 * sum(completions[excl]) / sum(completions))
```

> **Share of completions excluded by harmonisation: `r round(excl_pct$pct, 1)`%**

```{r show-ncver-annual, echo=FALSE}
ncver_annual %>% pivot_wider(names_from = remoteness, values_from = completions) %>%
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Table 6: Harmonised annual completions, Major City vs Regional", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"',
        format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

## 4. Combining demand and supply, and computing the divergence score

```{r combine}
combined <- ivi_annual %>%
  inner_join(ncver_annual, by = c("remoteness", "year")) %>%
  group_by(remoteness) %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(
    vacancy_growth    = (vacancies   - lag(vacancies))   / lag(vacancies)   * 100,
    completion_growth = (completions - lag(completions)) / lag(completions) * 100,
    divergence = vacancy_growth - completion_growth
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r show-combined, echo=FALSE}
combined %>%
  rename(
    Remoteness = remoteness, Year = year, Vacancies = vacancies, Completions = completions,
    `Vacancy growth %` = vacancy_growth, `Completion growth %` = completion_growth,
    `Divergence (pp)` = divergence
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.character(Year)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Table 7: Combined annual series with growth rates and divergence score", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"',
        digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

*NA = no prior year available for growth.*


The **divergence score** is defined as:

> **divergence (year t) = vacancy growth rate (year t) − completion growth rate (year t)**

A positive score means vacancy demand grew faster than training completions 
that year; a sustained positive and rising score signals a widening mismatch. 
A negative score means completions grew faster than vacancies. This is the core
novel contribution of the proposed system: existing resources compare demand and
supply *levels*, but, to our knowledge, none computes or tracks this 
*rate-of-change* signal over time.

## 5. Visualising the result

```{r plot-indexed, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
indexed <- combined %>%
  group_by(remoteness) %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(vac_index = vacancies / first(vacancies) * 100,
         comp_index = completions / first(completions) * 100) %>%
  select(remoteness, year, vac_index, comp_index) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(vac_index, comp_index), names_to = "series", values_to = "index") %>%
  mutate(series = recode(series, vac_index = "Vacancies (IVI)", comp_index = "Completions (NCVER)"))

ggplot(indexed, aes(x = year, y = index, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~remoteness) +
  labs(title = "Electricians: Vacancy Demand vs. Training Completions (Indexed, 2019 = 100)",
       x = NULL, y = "Index (2019 = 100)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r plot-divergence, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
div_data <- combined %>% filter(!is.na(divergence))

ggplot(div_data, aes(x = year, y = divergence, colour = remoteness)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Divergence Score: Vacancy Growth minus Completion Growth",
       subtitle = "Positive = demand outpacing training supply | Negative = supply catching up",
       x = NULL, y = "Divergence score (percentage points)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 6. Trend analysis

```{r trend}
trend_results <- lapply(unique(combined$remoteness), function(r) {
  sub <- combined %>% filter(remoteness == r, !is.na(divergence))
  fit <- lm(divergence ~ year, data = sub)
  s <- summary(fit)
  data.frame(
    Remoteness = r,
    `Slope (pp/year)` = round(coef(fit)[2], 2),
    `p-value` = round(s$coefficients[2, 4], 3),
    `R-squared` = round(s$r.squared, 3),
    n = nrow(sub),
    check.names = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()
rownames(trend_results) <- NULL
```

```{r show-trend, echo=FALSE}
kable(trend_results, caption = "Table 8: Linear trend fit, divergence score ~ year, by region", format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered"',
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#2C3E50")
```

## 7. Interpretation

For Electricians, the divergence score follows a consistent pattern in **both**
Major City and Regional areas: a large positive spike in 2021 (vacancies rebounded
far faster than training completions after the 2020 COVID dip), tapering through
2022-2023, and turning **negative** from 2024 onward (completions now growing
faster than vacancies in both regions). The fitted linear trend is negative for
both regions (approximately -6.4 to -6.6 percentage points per year), consistent
with a mismatch that is **narrowing** rather than widening over the observed
period - the opposite direction to a worsening shortage, and a genuinely useful
signal that a simple "current gap" comparison would not surface.

**Statistical caveat:** with only six year-over-year observations per region, the
trend slopes are not statistically significant at conventional thresholds
(p = 0.52 for Major City, p = 0.31 for Regional), and R-squared is modest. This is
expected given the sample size and the real-world volatility of the COVID-affected
period. The method is presented here as a **directional, feasibility-level
indicator** rather than a statistically validated forecast; a production version
of this system would need longer and more granular (e.g., quarterly) series to
support stronger statistical claims.

## 8. Feasibility conclusion

This demonstration confirms the core mechanism proposed in the project report is
technically feasible with real, publicly available Australian data:

1. Both data sources can be acquired, reshaped, and joined on a common
   occupation/region/year key.
2. A genuine divergence (rate-of-change) signal - not just a static level
   comparison - can be computed and visualised.
3. The resulting signal is interpretable and tells a substantively different
   story than either raw series alone: it correctly identifies that the
   Electricians training pipeline, after lagging during the COVID-era demand
   surge, has since caught up and is now outpacing vacancy growth.

A full production system would extend this single-occupation proof of concept
across the full ANZSCO occupation set, automate the NCVER DataBuilder extraction,
and incorporate quarterly or monthly completions data where available to improve
statistical power.
